title: Related Questions
question: Related Questions Q. assalamo alaikum,govt employees ko provident fund ka jo fix amount deduct hota hai har mahine ki salary se, wo retirement ke baad wapas milta hai asal amount se kuch percent zyada as a form of interest..kya wo extra amount jo interest ke form me hota hai use apne uper istemal kar sakte hai.agar nahi kar sakte hai to us paise ka kya karna chahiye. 2323 views Q. I am an Indian citizen. Can I take education loan from a non-Islamic bank inspite of knowing that I have to give the interest? - I have no other way to fund my higher education (MBA from a Australia). Please do mention any Islamic bank which can give me education loan in an Islamic way for my higher education (MBA) from US/Australia. 4104 views Q. AsSalaamu alaikum, I live in New Zealand with my wife and children. We live in a accommodation provided by government for poor people. The environment and people here are very bad. I am planning to move out in a better place.The rent outside is very high and if I buy a house then I have to borrow money from bank on interest. I have already searched for islamic finance but can't get one in this country.so plz tell me if i can take a loan from the bank for buying a house. JazakAllahu khair. 1923 views Q. Is bank loan permisible in India for business purpose? if yes what are the criteria and if no why? 2081 views Q. As salaamu alaykum Mufti Saheb, I have a query and hope you would be able to clarify the rule as per shariah. I did go through the past fatwa's on the website, however could not find soemthing which is similar to my query hence sending you this request. I had taken a car on loan in 2005. It had some down payment and the balance was to be paid in 60EMI's. I still have about another 2years more to pay this monthly instalments. What will be the best way to resolve this ,Should i clear the balance amount in one go if i can manage or if i do not have so much funds, should i sell off the car and pay off the money or what should be done. Jazakallah 1710 views Q. I was not aware of the prohibition of interest and gravity of its "hurmat". I came to Mumbai from Lucknow and started working in a Call Centre, I did not have my own house so I bought one by taking loan from a Bank. Now I realise the ill effects and evil of interest, I want to sell off that house and get rid of interest. I paid approximately Rs.1,30,000 out of my own pocket and got a loan of Rs.6,80,000, the house cost in all approximately Rs.8,10,000. Now I want to sell off that house, it may fetch around Rs.13 lakhs today. I want to know how much can I keep and how much will be the interest which I should not use. Please let me know out of the sale price how much will be HALAL for me and what percentage will be HARAM for me? Also let me know what could be the possible ways of disposing the HARAM amount. 1760 views Q. Loan and Interest Amount 4872 views Q. answer: Transactions & Dealings >> Interest & Insurance Question ID: 59496 Country: India Title: Home Loan Question: I want to build my house but I do not have that much money to do it so can it is permissible for me to take loan because I have one more brother and the house is so small and we have to get marriage and also my father has leaved us and married another woman and living with her so all the responsibilities are on me. So please answer me. Answer ID: 59496 Posted on: Aug 31, 2020 Bismillah hir-Rahman nir-Rahim ! (Fatwa: 887/883/B=09/1436) One should avoid taking loan from a bank so far as possible. It lands a man in several problems. It also brings the sin of paying interest. Yes, in case you are in dire need of a house and you are unable to find interest free debt then in compulsion it is allowable to take loan only as much as required. ويجوز للمحتاج الاستقراض بالربح . (الاشباه) Allah (Subhana Wa Ta'ala) knows Best Darul Ifta, Darul Uloom Deoband, India
